record.text: I keep coming across mathematics projects that bring knot theory to bear on physical field equations - studying how knots show up in the solution fields themselves, whether as knotted electromagnetic or magnetic field lines, knotted vortex lines and tubes in ideal fluid flows, or knotted nodal lines of quantum wavefunctions satisfying Maxwell's, Euler's or Schrodinger's equations. How do the projects working in this area differ in the physical systems and equations they focus on?
record.reference_answer: KNOTDYNAPP takes an electromagnetic and quantum-mechanical route: it proves that every knot type can occur as a stable closed field line of an electromagnetic field satisfying Maxwell's equations, constructs optical and quantum vortex knots as the knotted zeros of wavefunctions obeying Schrodinger and paraxial equations, and ties a knot's fiberedness to whether the magnetic field induced by a current through a knotted wire vanishes anywhere. GEOFLUIDS works instead in fluid mechanics and spectral theory, proving the Arnold-Moffatt conjecture on knotted vortex lines and Kelvin's conjecture on thin vortex tubes in Beltrami and steady Euler flows, and answering Berry's 2001 question by building Laplacian eigenfunctions whose nodal sets realize any knot type. FLUSPEC, a companion geometric-PDE program, targets smooth stationary solutions of the 3D Euler equations with chaotic trajectories confined in knotted vortex tubes of any topology, and studies vortex reconnection in the Gross-Pitaevskii equation. All three apply knot theory to solutions of physical field equations, but KNOTDYNAPP centres on electromagnetic field lines and quantum vortex knots whereas GEOFLUIDS and FLUSPEC centre on knotted vortex structures in incompressible fluid flows.
record.notes: Seeds: candidate cp2 vector-09 proposed KNOTDYNAPP(101023017)+BOPNIE(682537) via euroscivoc 'knot theory'. Reading BOPNIE(682537) shows it studies boundary value problems for nonlinear integrable PDEs; 'knot theory' appears once in a passing list of fields where integrable equations arise, and no knotted structure is studied - REJECTED as a euroscivoc false positive. KNOTDYNAPP is a genuine seed. Completeness sweep (non-embedding): run_sql objective LIKE '%knot%' returned the full 31-row universe; the only genuine knot-in-physical-field projects are KNOTDYNAPP(101023017), GEOFLUIDS(633152), FLUSPEC(862342); abstract-topology neighbours QuantGeomLangTFT(637618, TQFT knot invariants), LDTSing(101030083, algebraic/torus knots in 4-manifold surgery), MM-CAHF(893282, Heegaard Floer knot invariants), REFINV, OXTOP, GENERALIZED, ROGW all OUT (knots studied abstractly, no physical field); GOKNOT(796969, protein-backbone gordian knot via molecular dynamics) and MaCChines(787115, protein origami) OUT (discrete polymer, not a field-equation solution); euroscivoc 'knot theory' = {KNOTDYNAPP, BOPNIE}. Pooled adjudication (k=20, 37 candidates): IN KNOTDYNAPP (ranks L1/D1/H1/R1; EM field-line knots, quantum/optical vortex knots, fibered-knot vs induced magnetic field); IN GEOFLUIDS (L4/D2/H3/R2; knotted vortex lines/tubes in Beltrami/Euler flows, knotted nodal sets in QM); IN FLUSPEC (L2/D3/H2/R4; knotted vortex tubes of any topology in Euler flows, Gross-Pitaevskii vortex reconnection). OUT boundary candidates read in full: BOPNIE(682537) integrable-PDE BVPs; VORTSHEET(706283) 2D vortex sheets/patches, no knots; IPFLOW(725967) geodesic/Anosov flows and CFT, no knots; 3DWATERWAVES(678698) water waves over Beltrami flows, no knotted structures; HADE(669689) single vortex-filament equation/Talbot effect, no knot topology; GRAPHCPX(678156) graph-complex TQFT / rational homotopy of knot-spaces, abstract; TopMechMat(771503) 'knot' metaphorical (band-structure braiding); MM-CAHF(893282) abstract knot invariants. Remaining 34-3 rejected pooled candidates are integrable-systems / QFT / geometry projects with no knot topic (absent from the objective-'knot' universe). term_style=exact-term: all three gold retrieved by lexical (KNOTDYNAPP L1, FLUSPEC L2, GEOFLUIDS L4), confirming real term overlap with the question's borrowed vocabulary (knot theory, field lines, vortex tubes, nodal, Maxwell/Euler/Schrodinger). Level computed: |gold|=3 in [2,4] => L2. GEOFLUIDS and FLUSPEC are companion grants of the same fluid-knot program; both genuinely satisfy so both are kept, and the reference notes their kinship.

record.text: Which projects are aimed specifically at preventing, or detecting at an early stage, the skin and tissue damage that long periods of unrelieved pressure inflict on bedridden or wheelchair-bound patients?
record.reference_answer: Six H2020 grants in this corpus are aimed at this problem, and most are sensing-plus-prevention systems rather than treatments. i-LiveRest (696939) and its successor grant LiveRest (830134) put impedance, pressure, temperature and humidity textile sensors on a wheelchair or mattress to score Tissue Viability in real time and then trigger the prevention strategy that suits the user and context; their target group is Spinal Cord Injury patients, 85% of whom develop such an injury. Qone (735302) does the equivalent for bedridden patients with a pressure-relieving mattress carrying temperature and pressure mapping sensors feeding a personalised risk-score algorithm, claiming roughly a 75% reduction in new cases. The two JUMPAIR grants (709595, 783594) build a smart anti-decubitus mattress system that remotely tracks known ulcer-activity biomarkers to raise early alerts to the hospital. STINTS (811965) is the research and training strand: it studies the biomechanical and biochemical pathways by which prolonged pressure and shear destroy skin integrity, in order to improve preventative aids such as mattresses and insoles, early-stage diagnosis through non-invasive biomarkers and sensors, and ultrasound therapy.
record.notes:
SEEDS: cp6 candidate vector-68 (pressure injury / bedsores). Candidate evidence SQL re-executed this pass: the five-synonym ILIKE probe over project.title/objective still returns 11, no drift. Seed ids read in full: 696939, 709595, 735302, 783594, 811965, 815769, 830134, 834049, 845756, 868392, 869943.

BOUNDARY, ON THE FACE OF THE QUESTION: the question asks for projects 'aimed specifically at' preventing or early-detecting this damage. That wording, not the notes, decides the two boundaries where a survey gold set leaks. (a) Projects that heal an existing chronic wound are out, because healing is neither prevention nor early detection: 815769 LYSADERM (platelet-lysate cream for skin ulcers, pressure ulcers one of three indications), 869943 DERMAREP (eggshell-membrane dressing for pressure, leg and diabetic foot ulcers). (b) Projects whose own aim is something else, and for which this damage is a downstream application, are out: 845756 BIOCONTACT states 'the main objective of BIOCONTACT was to develop an advanced contact mechanics model able to accurately describe the contact behavior of elastic/viscoelastic thin layers', and reaches bedsores only as one benefit among contact lenses and prosthetic bones ('the accurate prediction of the contacting normal and tangential stresses acting on the soft biological tissues provides an efficient tool to reduce bedsores in long-term bedridden patients'). Every gold member's own stated aim IS this damage: prevention systems (696939, 830134, 735302, 709595, 783594) or the study of how prolonged pressure and shear destroy skin integrity in order to improve prevention and early diagnosis (811965).

JUMPAIR: 709595 (SME Phase 1, 2016) and 783594 (SME Phase 2, 2018) are two separate grants with the same acronym and distinct objectives; both are separately funded projects whose text satisfies the question, so both are gold. Same treatment for the i-LiveRest (696939) / LiveRest (830134) pair.

POOLED ADJUDICATION (final question string, k=20, all four conditions, 38 distinct projects). IN (6): 696939 i-LiveRest (real-time Tissue Viability sensing to prevent PU in wheelchair users); 830134 LiveRest (same system, written throughout as Pressure Injury, never pressure ulcer); 735302 Qone (sensing mattress predicting and preventing PU in bedridden patients); 783594 JUMPAIR (smart anti-decubitus system, biomarker monitoring for early diagnosis and prevention); 709595 JUMPAIR (Phase 1 of the same anti-decubitus system); 811965 STINTS (skin tissue integrity under prolonged pressure and shear; objectives are preventative aids, early-stage diagnosis, therapy). OUT (32): 845756 BIOCONTACT, 815769 LYSADERM and 869943 DERMAREP per the boundary above (LYSADERM did not surface in this run's pool but is adjudicated in the sweep list); 868392 Dignum (toilet assistive device, pressure ulcers only an inspection feature); 101003407 ELECTROSKIN, 873123 SWORD, 885973 StrataGRT, 833594 PHAS, 955722 SkinTERM, 892407 SKIN-REGEN-MECH, 877901 Bio2Skin - wound-healing, skin-graft, bandage or skin-adhesive work with pressure ulcers at most named in a chronic-wound list; 849047 and 826930 AGLYC (cardiac ischemia), 801126 EDIT (bladder cancer), 836268 DermoSafe 2.0 (skin cancer), 839888 MultiBioScan (tissue glycation imaging), 840786 BrainWatch (intracranial pressure implants), 101031327 WEARSENSNANO (hypothermia monitoring), 101038096 NeuroVascularHealth, 812772 Phys2BioMed, 885435 MAIT, 853508 BARRIER BREAK, 848158 EarlyCause, 101029808 EarlyCare, 101017385 WARIFA, 645759 WASTCArD - other conditions, matched on 'early detection' or 'tissue'; 643853 SC0806, 956003 REPAIRS, 745431 MyTherapyTools, 872082 ImpHandRehab, 855081 ABLE, 689476 RELIEF - rehabilitation/paralysis projects that name such damage at most as a complication they do not work on; 867161 ROCS (ore composition monitoring) - off-domain lexical match. Total: 6 + 32 = 38.

COMPLETENESS SWEEP (regexp_matches, case-folded, over project.title+objective AND report_text teaser+summary+workPerformed+finalResults+title; unchanged by the rewording, since it sweeps the topic's vocabulary and not the question string). record.text: In a project where a group of robots collectively assembled objects the way certain colony-dwelling animals build up their homes piece by piece, the robot that laid each piece could only sense a small region around itself at any moment. What hardware limitation forced its perception to stay so narrow?
record.reference_answer: The block-placing robot in this project - the BuilderBot - had to keep its field of view very small in order to stop its onboard CPU from overheating. As a result it could see only a few of the Stigmergic Blocks at a time, which limited the complexity of the structures it could build and the reliability of the building process.
record.notes: Seed: 846009 SRoCS (the only project in the euroscivoc 'swarm robotics' cluster, n=5, whose report documents a block-placing robot with a deliberately narrow field of view). L1 detail: the reason (field of view kept small to prevent CPU overheating) lives only in report_text.workPerformed, not in any stored column. Gold = seed only; |gold|=1 -> L1. Adjudication: pooled k=20 on the final wording surfaced 40 distinct projects across the four conditions; all 39 non-seed candidates OUT - industrial pick-and-place/assembly (PICKPLACE, LABOR, SYMBIO-TIC, GROW, VisionBot), space/planetary assembly (PRO-ACT, PULSAR, FACILITATORS), real-insect biology (ANTSolve, Ceratina, EMERG-ANT, Vision-In-Flight, HIVEOPOLIS), and swarm/collective robotics without the FOV-overheating fact (DEMIURGE, BROS, gAIa, SWARMs, CyBioSys); none describes a swarm-construction robot whose view was narrowed to prevent processor overheating. Completeness sweep (fact-based, wording-independent): run_sql over project.objective LIKE '%swarm%' AND (build|construct|assembl) -> 22 rows, only SRoCS is a swarm-robotics construction system; run_sql over report_text (workPerformed/summary/finalResults) LIKE '%overheat%' -> 68 rows, all battery/server/cooling/LED thermal projects, none a robot field-of-view constraint. No additional gold. term_style=paraphrase (reviewer WARN): the question avoids the answer terms (CPU, overheating) and the seed's key vocabulary (field of view; 'nest building behavior of social insects' rendered as 'colony-dwelling animals building up their homes'). On this final wording SRoCS is found by dense (rank 2), hybrid (1) and hybrid_rerank (1) but only drops to lexical rank 5 (it was lexical rank 1 under exact-term phrasing) - residual lexical overlap on generic robotics vocabulary keeps the paraphrase label borderline rather than clean dense-only evidence. index_fingerprint be84cbad9182 (n_vectors 190248, bge-base-en-v1.5).

record.text: Among the Horizon 2020 projects classified under superconductivity that received EU funding above the 95th percentile of all H2020 projects (about EUR 6.93 million in EC contribution), how do they differ in the application domain they target and in the way they make use of superconductivity?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT p.id, p.acronym, ROUND(p.ecMaxContribution) AS ec FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID=p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/superconductivity%' AND p.ecMaxContribution > 6926372.79 GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 3 DESC

record.reference_answer: All four are top-funded superconductivity projects but target sharply different domains. EcoSwing delivered the world's first demonstration of a high-temperature superconducting (HTS) direct-drive generator on a 3.6 MW wind turbine, using second-generation (2G) HTS wire coils to cut generator weight and rare-earth reliance in wind power. ARIES is a pan-European accelerator-infrastructure network that develops superconducting magnets, RF cavities with superconducting thin-film coatings, and cryogenics for particle accelerators and high-energy physics. NONLOCAL pursues fundamental quantum physics, engineering topological superconductivity and Majorana bound states in superconductor-semiconductor hybrid devices toward future quantum technologies, while HERO is a condensed-matter physics project searching for new hidden, entangled and resonating orders in correlated-electron quantum matter, where superconductivity figures as one example of the many-body paradigm rather than an engineered device.
record.notes: FILTER: P95 of project.ecMaxContribution over all 35,389 projects = 6926372.79 (re-executed this session via PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ecMaxContribution)). Superconductivity subtree matched with euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/superconductivity%' (paths carry no leading slash, per schema value note); subtree = 219 distinct projects; above-P95 survivors = exactly 4. TERM_STYLE exact-term: question reuses 'superconductivity/superconductor', distinctive vocabulary present in every gold text; scoped rank matrix shows all four gold found by the lexical condition, confirming real term overlap. PER-SURVIVOR ADJUDICATION (S=4, exhaustive read): 810451 HERO IN - condensed-matter/correlated-electron physics, 'hidden, entangled and resonating orders'; superconductivity cited as a paradigm example of quantum matter. 656024 EcoSwing IN - applied wind-energy domain; HTS direct-drive superconducting generator on a 3.6 MW turbine, 2G HTS wire coils. 730871 ARIES IN - particle-accelerator infrastructure; superconducting magnets, superconducting thin-film RF cavities, HTS tapes, cryogenics. 856526 NONLOCAL IN - fundamental quantum physics; topological superconductivity and Majorana bound states in superconductor-semiconductor hybrids for quantum technologies. All 4 IN => gold = all survivors. FILTER-LOAD-BEARING: unscoped pooled search on the textual theme is dominated by below-threshold superconductivity projects (EASITrain, SUPERTERA, SUPERSPIN, ULTRASUPERTAPE, ASuMED, etc., none in the survivor set); SQL sweep of superconductivity projects at/below P95 names concrete counter-examples that satisfy the textual theme but fail the funding filter: Quaco 689359 (4.65M, superconducting magnets for the LHC - same domain as ARIES), ASuMED 723119 (4.01M, superconducting aircraft propulsion motor), MATQu 101007322 (6.55M, superconducting qubits for quantum computing), AndQC 828948 (3.48M) and TOPSQUAD 862046 (3.18M, topological/Andreev-qubit quantum computing - same domain as NONLOCAL). 215 of the 219 superconductivity projects fall below the threshold, so the funding filter, not the topic, isolates the gold four. TEXT-LOAD-BEARING: application domain and superconductor technology live only in free text; euroSciVocTitle is 'superconductivity' for all four and no stored column encodes wind-generator vs accelerator-magnet vs Majorana vs hidden-order. SCOPED-RETRIEVABLE: scoped pooled top-k ranks EcoSwing/NONLOCAL/ARIES/HERO at 1-4 in lexical, hybrid and hybrid_rerank; HERO absent only from dense. Adjudication is from the exhaustive read; pooled_candidate_count is from the scoped pooled search.

record.text: Among graphene projects that include a Swedish participant, how do the ones tackling antibiotic-resistant bacterial infections make use of graphene?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID=p.id JOIN organization o ON o.projectID=p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%graphene%' AND o.country='SE'

record.reference_answer: Of the 18 graphene-classified projects with a Swedish participant, two attack antibiotic-resistant bacteria, and each puts graphene to a different use. PANG (Pathogen and Graphene) builds graphene-based antibacterial matrixes by chemically functionalising them with antibacterial peptides and molecules such as menthol, then exploits the photothermal properties of rGO in suspensions and transdermal patches - among them a flexible skin patch that treats subcutaneous wound infections under photothermal irradiation - to kill pathogens non-invasively, while also probing the effect of these structures on the immune system and their mechanism of action. PEST-BIN uses graphene on two fronts: infection diagnostic kits built as disposable 'plug-and-play' chips of graphene functionalised with receptors that capture bacterial-surface biomarkers, containing only carbon and biodegradable polymers and now produced by the spin-out LayerLogic AB; and antibacterial graphene coatings on magnetic nanoparticles and hydrogel/polymer coatings, loaded with antibiotics so that the resulting nano-weapon physically penetrates bacterial biofilms and delivers the drug inside them. Both therefore rely on graphene as an intrinsically antibacterial, functionalisable surface, PANG for light-triggered killing on the skin and PEST-BIN for sensing plus biofilm eradication.
record.notes: FILTER: euroSciVoc graphene subtree (euroSciVocPath LIKE '%graphene%'; profile note cp3 - paths carry no leading slash) intersected with any-role organization.country='SE'. Re-executed this pass: 18 survivors (candidate hybrid-02 evidence confirmed, no drift); graphene subtree corpus-wide is 290 projects, so the SE half prunes 290 -> 18. Survivors are enumerable (18 <= 200) so adjudication was EXHAUSTIVE: all 18 objectives read via get_project_text, plus a survivor-scoped SQL LIKE sweep over objective AND report_text (teaser||summary||workPerformed||finalResults) for bacter/antimicrob/antibiotic/pathogen/infection/biofilm - exactly 2 survivors hit, in both objective and report; the other 16 hit nothing in either field. OUT: 641416 iPUBLIC (inkjet-printed graphene energy storage); 646155 INSPIRED (graphene nanoplatelet inks for printed electronics); 650029 TAIPI (CSA on Flagship impact assessment); 686135 PROCETS (anti-wear/anti-corrosion coatings); 696656 GrapheneCore1, 785219 GrapheneCore2, 881603 GrapheneCore3 (Flagship umbrella projects - composites, photonics, batteries, neural electrodes; no antibacterial work in objective or report); 721991 GreenCarbon (biomass-derived carbons for CO2 capture/catalysis); 758935 1D-Engine (theory of 1D electrons and superconductivity); 764977 mCBEEs (corrosion of micro/nano devices); 810451 HERO (hidden order in quantum matter); 824962 Car2TERA (sub-THz radar and graphene MMICs); 952792 2D-EPL (2D pilot line wafer prototyping); 101002772 SPINNER (graphene spintronics); 101006963 GreEnergy (graphene rectennas for energy harvesting); 101017186 AEOLUS (mid-IR photonic gas sensing). Dropping the SE half would therefore change the answer set - filter is load-bearing. record.text: Among ERC Starting Grant projects on nanoscale light control, which one set out to do away with the lenses and reflectors added onto low-energy lamps by placing the light-emitting nanoparticles inside engineered surroundings - stacked layers, patterned surfaces and resonant cavities - so that the tint and the beam spread of the light are fixed by those surroundings rather than by changing what the particles themselves are made of?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/nanophotonics%' AND p.fundingScheme = 'ERC-STG'

record.reference_answer: NANOPHOM (project 715832) is the ERC Starting Grant in question: it puts rare-earth nanophosphors inside engineered optical structures - multilayers, surface textures, nano-scatterers, nanoimprinted corrugations and optical cavities - and shows that those surroundings alone set the chromaticity and the directionality of the device's output, 'without modifying the chemical composition of the emitters', replacing the reflectors and lenses normally added as secondary optical elements. Its target demonstrations were directional white-light emission within a narrow angular cone and omnidirectional emission of monochromatic light.
record.notes: FILTER: euroSciVoc leaf 'nanophotonics' (one-reading check: 'engineering and technology/nanotechnology/nanophotonics' is the only path matching '%nanophotonics%', 62 projects) intersected with fundingScheme='ERC-STG' -> 10 survivors, re-executed this pass. Runtime note: the scoped path (src/retrieval/scoped.py) can only filter the structural half ('ERC Starting Grant' -> fundingScheme='ERC-STG'); the nanophotonics topic is carried by retrieval, which is how the question is worded. LOW note on scope width: the enumerated survivor set is narrower than the runtime's executable scope (all ERC-STG projects), so ERC-STG projects tagged under other euroSciVoc leaves - e.g. 849229 CQWLED (nanocrystals / colors / optoelectronics) - are reachable at runtime but not enumerated here; CQWLED is excluded by the question's own words (see ADJUDICATION), so this is a recorded width note, not a gold gap.
